facts.text: Campbell River hosts the headquarters of three major farmed-salmon producers: Cermaq Canada, Mowi Canada West and Grieg Seafood BC.
facts.evidence: The city hosts the headquarters of three major farmed-salmon producers: Cermaq Canada, Mowi Canada West, and Grieg Seafood BC.

facts.text: The aquaculture industry employs more than 400 people in Campbell River alone, with hundreds more from smaller North Island communities.
facts.evidence: The aquaculture industry employs more than 400 people in Campbell River alone, with hundreds more employed from smaller communities on the North Island.

facts.text: The federal government has mandated an end to open-net fish farming in coastal BC by 2029, creating uncertainty for Campbell River's aquaculture sector.

facts.text: Forestry still employs about 6 percent of Campbell River's labour force.

overview: Campbell River had 35,519 residents in the 2021 Census, up 7.6 percent from 33,007 in 2016, in 15,557 occupied homes across 144.38 square kilometres. It serves as a regional centre for the North Island, so local businesses often draw customers from smaller communities nearby.

The economy rests on salmon farming, forestry and tourism. Aquaculture headquarters and suppliers create business-to-business demand, while sport fishing and outdoor recreation bring visitors through the city.
